briefs.planning:
Create one finished static English screen for Beacon, a municipal library staffing planner. At 09:10 a coordinator must decide how to cover the afternoon desks. Deliver a self-contained index.html and a PNG at exactly 1440 × 900 CSS pixels, no scrolling. Do not implement interactions or extra screens.
Show all six branches and these exact facts for 13:00–17:00: North needs 3 staff, assigned 2, certified lead present; Canal needs 2, assigned 2, lead present; Market needs 3, assigned 3, lead absent; Hill needs 2, assigned 1, lead absent; Park needs 2, assigned 2, lead present; East needs 2, assigned 2, lead present. A staffed branch still requires a certified lead. A lead can fill a staff place. Staff can cover only one branch during this interval.
Show these available people: Ana — certified lead, available 13:00–17:00, can reach Hill in 15 min or Market in 25 min; Ben — not a lead, available 13:00–17:00, can reach North in 20 min; Chi — certified lead, only available 15:00–17:00, can reach Market in 10 min. The selected branch is Hill. Give the selected branch its relevant details and a clear proposed next action, while preserving the coordinator's view of all shortages and unresolved lead coverage. Show last update 09:08 and the date 29 October 2026. Demonstration data must be identified discreetly.
Choose the visual direction and layout. Prioritize a clear, credible work surface that helps the coordinator make a sound assignment. Do not add fake forecasts, charts, invented readiness scores or data beyond what is needed to present the supplied facts. Include a short decisions.md with decisions and checks actually performed.
briefs.festival:
Create one finished typographic poster for a fictional festival called SHIFT / CHANGE, celebrating repair, reuse and the visible history of objects. Deliver a self-contained index.html and one PNG at exactly 900 × 1200 pixels. Static, no scrolling, no application controls. UI/copy in English.
Exact details: Saturday 28 November 2026; 11:00–19:00; Foundry Rooms, 8 Mill Lane. Programme: 11:30 Repair as a Practice — talk by Mara Lin; 14:00 Second Life Objects — exhibition walkthrough; 16:30 The Visible Seam — live textile repair; 18:00 Objects After Dark — sound performance. Entry €12; under 16 free. Bring one small broken object for the repair table, open 12:00–16:00; repairs are not guaranteed. Include all practical details and identify this as a fictional event discreetly.
The audience is curious adults who enjoy design and making. The poster should feel distinctive and well composed, without mimicking a dashboard. Choose a visual idea based on repair, joining or change. Use type, CSS or simple SVG geometry; no photographs or generated images. Avoid invented sponsors, attendance figures or extra events. Include a short decisions.md with decisions and checks actually performed.
